admission.justification: The direction weighed the v1 Orchestrator default and direct Architect coordination as real alternatives, and the choice constrains every later change to the role texts, the router and the manifest.

alternatives.option: One Manager is the Architect's coordinator for a single master; an Orchestrator sits above the Managers only when two or more masters are worked on at the same time and starts one Manager per master; the developer may still choose direct coordination or a single-master Orchestrator.
alternatives.reason: A Manager that decides its own master removes the relay that left the Architect unresponsive, while the Orchestrator remains for genuinely concurrent masters.

alternatives.option: Keep MIK-R72@v1's default: the Architect's first delegation is one Orchestrator directly under it for every delegated master.
alternatives.reason: The developer withdrew it after the Orchestrator relayed extensively and the Architect became unresponsive (D57).
alternatives.reconsider_when: A Manager under one master repeatedly cannot keep the work moving without an Orchestrator above it.

alternatives.option: Keep the master line's default: the Architect coordinates directly and inserts no coordinating agent.
alternatives.reason: The Architect coordinated a Manager itself and did not answer the developer (D52); direct coordination stays only as the developer's explicit choice.
alternatives.reconsider_when: The developer chooses direct coordination for a single small leaf and the Architect stays responsive.

consequences: The Architect, Manager, Orchestrator, planning and coordination texts and the four manifest descriptions state the same default and the same two developer choices.
A plan delta no longer returns to the agent that started the Manager by default; only the four developer-needed categories and the final report do.
The default is advice, not a start-permission change; no tool refuses an Orchestrator above a single master.
context: MIK-R72@v1 made an Orchestrator the default for every delegation after the developer's direction D52. In the same run the Orchestrator sent the Architect a dozen ruling requests and notices in two hours (D57), and on 2026-10-05 the Architect coordinated directly and did not answer the developer. On 2026-10-06 the developer named the cause (D66): the Manager passed everything up instead of managing, so an Orchestrator is only needed when two or more masters run at a time.
decider: The developer (D52, D57, D66) and the architect's approved MIK-R72@v2 packet; D66 supersedes v1.
